This book follows five Xenium analysis vignettes in the requested order. It
starts with cell segmentation polygons, measures their geometry, compares
Delaunay and polygon proximity graphs, explores the distance threshold, and
finishes with close-up views of direct neighbors. Each numbered chapter
corresponds to one vignette.

The chapters share one R session. Packages, data, plotting helpers, spatial
metrics, and neighbor candidates are prepared once and reused. The HTML
contains its figures and animation, so it can be read offline.

# Before you begin {.unnumbered}

## Paths and execution {.unnumbered}

Keep this source file in the project's `Book` folder. The original dataset is
read from `../data`; new figures, animation frames, and result tables are saved
inside `Book`. All R chunks are evaluated and their code is displayed. An R
error stops the render.

```{r book-paths, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
book_dir <- normalizePath(
  dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)),
  winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE
)
project_root <- normalizePath(
  file.path(book_dir, ".."), winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE
)
figure_dir <- file.path(book_dir, "figures")
frame_dir <- file.path(book_dir, "frames")
result_dir <- file.path(book_dir, "results")
for (directory in c(figure_dir, frame_dir, result_dir)) {
  dir.create(directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = book_dir)
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
options(timeout = max(600, getOption("timeout")))
set.seed(42)
```

## Check and load packages {.unnumbered}

Check each dependency before installing it. Missing packages are installed
into a project-local library. Existing installations are reused. `microbiome`
comes from Bioconductor; `RGraphSpace` is installed from its development
repository if the required version is unavailable. Seurat, gridExtra, and
ggpubr are unnecessary here because the book uses the GraphSpace object
directly and combines plots with patchwork.

```{r book-packages, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
local_library <- file.path(book_dir, "_R_library")
if (dir.exists(local_library)) {
  .libPaths(c(local_library, .libPaths()))
}
prepare_local_library <- function() {
  dir.create(local_library, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  .libPaths(c(local_library, .libPaths()))
  local_library
}

cran_packages <- c(
  "knitr", "rmarkdown", "sf", "ggplot2", "dplyr",
  "patchwork", "psych", "lwgeom", "deldir", "igraph", "gifski", "ragg",
  "BiocManager", "remotes"
)
for (package in cran_packages) {
  if (!requireNamespace(package, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(package, lib = prepare_local_library())
  }
}
if (!requireNamespace("microbiome", quietly = TRUE)) {
  BiocManager::install(
    "microbiome", lib = prepare_local_library(), ask = FALSE, update = FALSE
  )
}
if (!requireNamespace("RGraphSpace", quietly = TRUE) ||
    utils::packageVersion("RGraphSpace") < "1.5.4") {
  remotes::install_github(
    "sysbiolab/RGraphSpace", lib = prepare_local_library(),
    upgrade = "never", build_vignettes = FALSE
  )
}

required_packages <- c(cran_packages, "microbiome", "RGraphSpace")
available <- vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
if (!all(available)) {
  stop("Unavailable packages: ", paste(required_packages[!available], collapse = ", "))
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(RGraphSpace)
  library(sf)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(dplyr)
  library(patchwork)
})
package_versions <- data.frame(
  package = required_packages,
  version = vapply(required_packages, function(x) {
    as.character(utils::packageVersion(x))
  }, character(1))
)
knitr::kable(package_versions, caption = "Dependencies used for this render")
write.csv(package_versions, file.path(result_dir, "package-versions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Load and validate the crop {.unnumbered}

Download the crop only when it is missing. Check the object class, required
columns, cell identifiers, and polygon geometry before proceeding. The crop
uses normalized planar coordinates without a geographic coordinate reference
system: the distance thresholds below are in these coordinate units, not
micrometers. Areas and perimeters have the corresponding normalized units.

```{r book-data, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
data_dir <- file.path(project_root, "data")
dir.create(data_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
data_file <- file.path(data_dir, "Xenium_GS_Crop.RDS")
data_url <- paste0(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flaviogckessler/Curso_ST/",
  "main/data/Xenium_GS_Crop.RDS"
)
if (!file.exists(data_file)) {
  utils::download.file(data_url, data_file, mode = "wb")
}
gs_crop <- readRDS(data_file)
stopifnot(inherits(gs_crop, "GraphSpace"))
required_columns <- c("vertex", "name", "x", "y", "geometry", "nCount_Xenium", "nFeature_Xenium")
stopifnot(all(required_columns %in% names(gs_crop@nodes)))
stopifnot(nrow(gs_crop@nodes) >= 9L, igraph::ecount(gs_crop@graph) == 0L)
cell_names <- as.character(gs_vertex_attr(gs_crop, "name"))
stopifnot(!anyNA(cell_names), !anyDuplicated(cell_names))
cell_geometry <- sf::st_geometry(sf::st_as_sf(gs_crop@nodes))
stopifnot(
  all(sf::st_is_valid(cell_geometry)),
  !any(sf::st_is_empty(cell_geometry)),
  all(as.character(sf::st_geometry_type(cell_geometry)) %in% c("POLYGON", "MULTIPOLYGON"))
)
if (isTRUE(sf::st_is_longlat(cell_geometry))) {
  stop("This workflow requires planar tissue coordinates.")
}
stopifnot(
  nrow(gs_crop@fdata) == length(cell_names),
  !is.null(rownames(gs_crop@fdata)),
  setequal(rownames(gs_crop@fdata), cell_names),
  "Slc17a7" %in% colnames(gs_crop@fdata)
)
proximity_threshold <- 0.0005
distance_grid <- seq(from = 0, to = 0.002, by = 0.0001)
cpal <- grDevices::hcl.colors(100, palette = "Spectral", rev = TRUE)
data_range <- c(0, 7)
my_theme <- theme_gspace_coords(
  theme = "th3", is_norm = TRUE,
  xlab = "Tissue coordinate 1", ylab = "Tissue coordinate 2"
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  cells = length(cell_names), genes = ncol(gs_crop@fdata),
  initial_edges = igraph::ecount(gs_crop@graph),
  selected_distance = proximity_threshold
), caption = "Input crop")
```

# Inspecting neighbors {#sec-inspecting-neighbors}

Based on `Vignettes/InspectingNeighbors.Rmd`.

Cell segmentation polygons can identify nearby cells even when their boundaries
do not overlap. This chapter compares polygon intersection with a small
distance tolerance using the first nine cells of the crop.

## A reusable cell plot

Define the common plotting and saving functions once. Later chapters change
the layers and their appearance through arguments, using the same palette
and coordinate theme. Overview networks and animation frames use vectorized
line segments. Detailed GraphSpace edge glyphs are used for the close-up
styling examples in Chapter 5.

```{r cell-plot-helper, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
edge_layer <- function(gs, colour = "black", alpha = 0.6) {
  edges <- igraph::as_data_frame(gs@graph, what = "edges")
  names <- as.character(gs_vertex_attr(gs, "name"))
  from <- match(edges$from, names)
  to <- match(edges$to, names)
  segments <- data.frame(
    x = gs@nodes$x[from], y = gs@nodes$y[from],
    xend = gs@nodes$x[to], yend = gs@nodes$y[to]
  )
  geom_segment(
    data = segments, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = colour, alpha = alpha, linewidth = 0.2
  )
}
plot_cells <- function(gs, polygons = TRUE, nodes = TRUE, edges = FALSE,
                       colour_by_expression = TRUE, edge_colour = "black",
                       edge_alpha = 0.6, node_size = 0.2, node_alpha = 1,
                       title = NULL, edge_engine = c("segments", "graphspace")) {
  edge_engine <- match.arg(edge_engine)
  native_edges <- edge_engine == "graphspace"
  if (native_edges) {
    p <- ggplot(gs)
  } else {
    plot_data <- sf::st_as_sf(gs@nodes)
    expression_rows <- match(as.character(plot_data$name), rownames(gs@fdata))
    stopifnot(!anyNA(expression_rows))
    plot_data$Slc17a7 <- as.numeric(gs@fdata[expression_rows, "Slc17a7"])
    p <- ggplot(plot_data)
  }
  if (polygons) {
    if (colour_by_expression) {
      p <- p + geom_sf(
        aes(geometry = geometry, fill = log2(Slc17a7 + 1)),
        colour = "grey65", linewidth = 0.05
      ) + scale_fill_gradientn(colours = cpal, limits = data_range, name = "log2(Slc17a7 + 1)")
    } else {
      p <- p + geom_sf(aes(geometry = geometry), fill = "grey92", linewidth = 0.08)
    }
  }
  if (edges && igraph::ecount(gs@graph) > 0L) {
    p <- p + if (native_edges) {
      geom_edgespace(colour = edge_colour, alpha = edge_alpha)
    } else {
      edge_layer(gs, colour = edge_colour, alpha = edge_alpha)
    }
  }
  if (nodes) {
    if (!polygons && colour_by_expression) {
      layer <- if (native_edges) {
        geom_nodespace(aes(colour = log2(Slc17a7 + 1)),
                       size = node_size, pch = 19, alpha = node_alpha)
      } else {
        geom_point(aes(x = x, y = y, colour = log2(Slc17a7 + 1)),
                    size = node_size, pch = 19, alpha = node_alpha)
      }
      p <- p + layer + scale_colour_gradientn(
        colours = cpal, limits = data_range, name = "log2(Slc17a7 + 1)"
      )
    } else {
      layer <- if (native_edges) {
        geom_nodespace(colour = "black", size = node_size, pch = 19, alpha = node_alpha)
      } else {
        geom_point(aes(x = x, y = y), colour = "black",
                    size = node_size, pch = 19, alpha = node_alpha)
      }
      p <- p + layer
    }
  }
  if (native_edges) {
    p <- p + my_theme
  } else {
    p <- p + (if (polygons) coord_sf(datum = NA) else coord_equal()) +
      theme_minimal() + labs(x = "Tissue coordinate 1", y = "Tissue coordinate 2")
  }
  p + labs(title = title)
}
save_figure <- function(plot, filename, width = 9, height = 6) {
  ggplot2::ggsave(
    filename = file.path(figure_dir, filename), plot = plot,
    width = width, height = height, units = "in", dpi = 120, bg = "white"
  )
}
```

```{r crop-expression, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
expression_view <- plot_cells(gs_crop, polygons = FALSE, node_size = 1)
segmentation_view <- plot_cells(gs_crop)
expression_view + segmentation_view +
  plot_annotation(title = "Cell coordinates and segmentation", tag_levels = "A")
```

## Inspect polygon types and intersections

The sparse list returned by `st_intersects()` contains the indices of each
polygon's neighbors. Exclude self-intersections explicitly. Using the neighbor
list directly also avoids a many-to-many join that repeats cell geometries.

```{r inspect-intersections, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(sf::st_geometry_type(cell_geometry))),
             col.names = c("Geometry", "Cells"))
example_cells <- sf::st_as_sf(gs_crop@nodes[seq_len(9L), ])
intersect_list <- sf::st_intersects(example_cells, remove_self = TRUE)
neighbor_table <- function(neighbor_list) {
  data.frame(
    cell = seq_along(neighbor_list),
    neighbors = vapply(neighbor_list, function(x) paste(x, collapse = ", "), character(1)),
    count = lengths(neighbor_list)
  )
}
knitr::kable(neighbor_table(intersect_list), caption = "Neighbors from polygon intersection")

plot_neighbor_status <- function(cells, neighbor_list, title) {
  cells$status <- factor(
    ifelse(lengths(neighbor_list) > 0L, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes")
  )
  ggplot(cells) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = status), linewidth = 0.3, show.legend = TRUE) +
    geom_text(aes(x = x, y = y, label = vertex), size = 3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(Yes = "#2b8cbe", No = "grey85"), drop = FALSE) +
    theme_minimal() + labs(title = title, fill = "Has neighbor?", x = "x", y = "y")
}
intersection_plot <- plot_neighbor_status(example_cells, intersect_list, "Intersecting polygons")
```

## Neighbors within a distance

`st_is_within_distance()` compares the minimum distance between polygons with
the chosen tolerance. It does not require their original boundaries to overlap.
For the visual illustration, buffer each polygon by **half** the tolerance:
expanding both polygons by the full tolerance would illustrate twice the
intended separation. Curved buffers are approximations; neighbor status always
comes from the distance predicate itself.

```{r inspect-distance-neighbors, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7}
neighbor_list <- sf::st_is_within_distance(
  example_cells, dist = proximity_threshold, remove_self = TRUE
)
knitr::kable(neighbor_table(neighbor_list), caption = "Neighbors within the selected distance")
distance_plot <- plot_neighbor_status(example_cells, neighbor_list, "Within distance tolerance")
buffered_cells <- sf::st_buffer(example_cells, dist = proximity_threshold / 2)
buffer_plot <- plot_neighbor_status(buffered_cells, neighbor_list, "Half-distance buffers")
neighbor_inspection <- intersection_plot + distance_plot + buffer_plot +
  plot_layout(ncol = 1, guides = "collect") + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
neighbor_inspection
save_figure(neighbor_inspection, "InspectingNeighbors.png", width = 10, height = 7)
```

# Polygon geometry {#sec-polygon-geometry}

Based on `Vignettes/polygonGeometry.Rmd`.

Measure polygon area, diameter, and perimeter for the full crop. Store these
features on the GraphSpace object so the remaining chapters can reuse them.

## Calculate spatial metrics once

The diameter is the maximum Euclidean distance between polygon vertices.
Remove duplicate closing vertices rather than discarding a vertex by position.
`lwgeom::st_perimeter_lwgeom()` supplies the polygon perimeter explicitly.

```{r spatial-metrics, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
maxDistPol <- function(polygon) {
  vertices <- unique(sf::st_coordinates(polygon)[, c("X", "Y"), drop = FALSE])
  if (nrow(vertices) < 2L) return(0)
  max(stats::dist(vertices))
}
metric_names <- c("area", "perimeter", "maxDist")
spatial_metrics <- data.frame(
  cell = cell_names,
  area = as.numeric(sf::st_area(cell_geometry)),
  perimeter = as.numeric(lwgeom::st_perimeter_lwgeom(cell_geometry)),
  maxDist = vapply(seq_along(cell_geometry), function(i) {
    maxDistPol(cell_geometry[i])
  }, numeric(1))
)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(as.matrix(spatial_metrics[metric_names]))))
stopifnot(all(as.matrix(spatial_metrics[metric_names]) > 0))
for (metric in metric_names) {
  gs_vertex_attr(gs_crop, metric) <- spatial_metrics[[metric]]
}
meanMaxDist <- mean(spatial_metrics$maxDist)
write.csv(spatial_metrics, file.path(result_dir, "cell-spatial-metrics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(summary(spatial_metrics[metric_names]), digits = 6)
```

```{r metric-distributions, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
plot_distribution <- function(data, feature, label) {
  ggplot(data, aes(x = "", y = .data[[feature]])) +
    geom_violin(fill = "#d2e8e7", colour = "#285e67") +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.size = 0.35, alpha = 0.6) +
    theme_minimal() + labs(x = NULL, y = label)
}
metric_plots <- lapply(metric_names, function(metric) {
  plot_distribution(spatial_metrics, metric, metric)
})
spatial_feature_plot <- wrap_plots(metric_plots, nrow = 1) +
  plot_annotation(title = "Cell polygon spatial metrics")
spatial_feature_plot
save_figure(spatial_feature_plot, "SpatialFeatures_RawCrop.png", width = 10, height = 4)
plot_distribution(gs_crop@nodes, "nCount_Xenium", "Xenium counts") +
  plot_distribution(gs_crop@nodes, "nFeature_Xenium", "Detected features")
```

## Correlate expression with spatial features

To retain the analysis in the vignette, these are correlations with the **raw
expression counts** stored in the crop. They are exploratory: library size,
cell area, cropping, and spatial dependence can affect the associations. A
normalized expression analysis on the full tissue is a useful follow-up.

Align expression rows to cell identifiers explicitly and remove genes with no
variation. Calculate both methods through one function. Adjust P-values over
all gene-by-feature tests within each method using Benjamini-Hochberg.

```{r correlation-analysis, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
expr <- as.matrix(gs_crop@fdata)
expr <- expr[match(cell_names, rownames(expr)), , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(identical(rownames(expr), cell_names), all(is.finite(expr)))
variable_genes <- apply(expr, 2, stats::sd) > 0
expr <- expr[, variable_genes, drop = FALSE]
meta <- spatial_metrics[metric_names]
stopifnot(ncol(expr) > 0L, all(vapply(meta, stats::sd, numeric(1)) > 0))

correlate_features <- function(method) {
  fit <- psych::corr.test(
    x = expr, y = meta, method = method,
    adjust = "none", use = "pairwise", ci = FALSE
  )
  result <- as.data.frame(as.table(fit$r), responseName = "correlation")
  names(result)[1:2] <- c("gene", "feature")
  result$gene <- as.character(result$gene)
  result$feature <- factor(result$feature, levels = metric_names)
  result$p_value <- as.vector(fit$p)
  result$p_adjusted <- stats::p.adjust(result$p_value, method = "BH")
  result$method <- method
  result
}
correlation_results <- setNames(
  lapply(c("pearson", "spearman"), correlate_features), c("pearson", "spearman")
)
all_correlations <- dplyr::bind_rows(correlation_results)
write.csv(all_correlations, file.path(result_dir, "expression-spatial-correlations.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  cells = nrow(expr), variable_genes = ncol(expr), spatial_features = ncol(meta),
  tests_per_method = ncol(expr) * ncol(meta)
), caption = "Correlation analysis dimensions")
```

## Plot the significant associations

Use a single rule for both methods: adjusted P-value below 0.01 and absolute
correlation of at least 0.3. Symmetric color limits retain negative
associations. Each heatmap derives its gene order from its own results. If no
associations pass the filters, show that result instead of failing during
plotting.

```{r correlation-heatmaps, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 9}
alpha <- 0.01
minimum_correlation <- 0.3
plot_correlations <- function(result, method) {
  selected <- dplyr::filter(
    result, is.finite(correlation), !is.na(p_adjusted),
    p_adjusted < alpha, abs(correlation) >= minimum_correlation
  )
  if (nrow(selected) == 0L) {
    return(ggplot() + annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0, label = "No associations pass the filters") +
             theme_void() + labs(title = paste(method, "correlations")))
  }
  gene_order <- selected |>
    dplyr::group_by(gene) |>
    dplyr::summarise(strength = max(abs(correlation)), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::arrange(strength, gene) |>
    dplyr::pull(gene)
  microbiome::heat(
    as.data.frame(selected), "feature", "gene", fill = "correlation",
    star = "p_adjusted", p.adj.threshold = alpha,
    association.threshold = minimum_correlation, filter.significant = FALSE,
    order.rows = FALSE, order.cols = FALSE,
    colours = c("#2166ac", "white", "#b2182b"), limits = c(-1, 1),
    legend.text = method
  ) + scale_x_discrete(limits = metric_names) + scale_y_discrete(limits = gene_order) +
    labs(title = paste(method, "expression versus polygon geometry"),
         caption = "BH-adjusted P < 0.01; absolute correlation >= 0.3", x = NULL, y = NULL)
}
for (method in names(correlation_results)) {
  heatmap <- plot_correlations(correlation_results[[method]], method)
  print(heatmap)
  save_figure(heatmap, paste0(method, "-spatial-correlations.png"), width = 7, height = 9)
}
significant_correlations <- dplyr::filter(
  all_correlations, p_adjusted < alpha, abs(correlation) >= minimum_correlation
)
write.csv(significant_correlations, file.path(result_dir, "significant-correlations.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(significant_correlations$method)),
             col.names = c("Method", "Significant gene-feature pairs"))
```

## Polygon centers

A mathematical centroid can lie outside a concave polygon.
`st_point_on_surface()` supplies an interior point. The existing GraphSpace
coordinates are retained throughout the network comparisons.

```{r polygon-centers, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
example_geometry <- sf::st_geometry(example_cells)
center_comparison <- data.frame(
  cell = example_cells$vertex,
  centroid_inside = diag(sf::st_within(
    sf::st_centroid(example_geometry), example_geometry, sparse = FALSE
  )),
  surface_point_inside = diag(sf::st_within(
    sf::st_point_on_surface(example_geometry), example_geometry, sparse = FALSE
  ))
)
knitr::kable(center_comparison)
```

# Delaunay and proximity networks {#sec-delaunay-network}

Based on `Vignettes/DelaunayNet.Rmd`.

Delaunay triangulation uses the cell coordinates. The proximity graph uses
distances between segmentation polygons. Both graphs retain the same cell
identifiers, so their edges can be compared as labeled cell pairs.

## Build the Delaunay graph

```{r delaunay-graph, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
xy <- as.matrix(gs_crop@nodes[, c("x", "y")])
stopifnot(all(is.finite(xy)), !anyDuplicated(as.data.frame(xy)))
triangulation <- deldir::deldir(xy[, 1], xy[, 2], suppressMsge = TRUE)
triangulation_indices <- triangulation$delsgs[, c("ind1", "ind2")]
delaunay_edges <- data.frame(
  from = cell_names[triangulation_indices$ind1],
  to = cell_names[triangulation_indices$ind2]
)
gs_crop_dnay <- gs_add_edges(gs_crop, delaunay_edges)
gs_edge_attr(gs_crop_dnay, "arrowType") <- 0
stopifnot(
  igraph::ecount(gs_crop_dnay@graph) == nrow(delaunay_edges),
  igraph::is_simple(gs_crop_dnay@graph)
)
knitr::kable(utils::head(delaunay_edges), caption = "Delaunay edges mapped to cell names")
```

## Prepare reusable proximity candidates

Find candidate pairs once at the largest distance used in the book. Compute
their exact polygon distances and retain one row per undirected pair. Any
smaller threshold can then filter this table without repeating a full spatial
query. The helper checks its distance range and cell identifiers before adding
edges.

```{r proximity-helper, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
maximum_distance <- max(distance_grid)
candidate_neighbors <- sf::st_is_within_distance(
  cell_geometry, dist = maximum_distance, remove_self = TRUE
)
candidate_indices <- data.frame(
  from_index = rep(seq_along(candidate_neighbors), lengths(candidate_neighbors)),
  to_index = unlist(candidate_neighbors, use.names = FALSE)
)
candidate_indices <- candidate_indices[
  candidate_indices$from_index < candidate_indices$to_index, , drop = FALSE
]
proximity_candidates <- data.frame(
  from = cell_names[candidate_indices$from_index],
  to = cell_names[candidate_indices$to_index],
  distance = as.numeric(sf::st_distance(
    cell_geometry[candidate_indices$from_index],
    cell_geometry[candidate_indices$to_index], by_element = TRUE
  ))
)
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(proximity_candidates[c("from", "to")]),
  all(is.finite(proximity_candidates$distance)),
  all(proximity_candidates$distance <= maximum_distance + 1e-12)
)
gs_neighbors <- function(gs, dist) {
  stopifnot(length(dist) == 1L, is.finite(dist), dist >= 0, dist <= maximum_distance)
  stopifnot(identical(as.character(gs_vertex_attr(gs, "name")), cell_names))
  stopifnot(igraph::ecount(gs@graph) == 0L)
  edges <- proximity_candidates[
    proximity_candidates$distance <= dist, c("from", "to"), drop = FALSE
  ]
  if (nrow(edges) == 0L) return(gs)
  result <- gs_add_edges(gs, edges)
  gs_edge_attr(result, "arrowType") <- 0
  stopifnot(igraph::is_simple(result@graph), igraph::ecount(result@graph) == nrow(edges))
  result
}
gs_crop_prox <- gs_neighbors(gs_crop, dist = proximity_threshold)
write.csv(proximity_candidates, file.path(result_dir, "proximity-candidate-distances.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Compare the graph views

The polygon diameters calculated in Chapter 2 are already attached to both
graph objects. Plot segmentation, cell coordinates, and the two edge sets.

```{r network-comparison, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 10}
network_panels <- list(
  plot_cells(gs_crop, colour_by_expression = FALSE, title = "Cell segmentation"),
  plot_cells(gs_crop, polygons = FALSE, colour_by_expression = FALSE,
             node_size = 0.4, title = "Cell coordinates"),
  plot_cells(gs_crop_dnay, polygons = FALSE, edges = TRUE,
             colour_by_expression = FALSE, title = "Delaunay triangulation"),
  plot_cells(gs_crop_prox, polygons = FALSE, edges = TRUE,
             colour_by_expression = FALSE, title = "Polygon proximity")
)
delaunay_figure <- wrap_plots(network_panels[1:3], nrow = 1) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
network_comparison <- wrap_plots(network_panels, ncol = 2) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
network_comparison
save_figure(delaunay_figure, "GraphSpace_Delaunay.png", width = 12, height = 4)
save_figure(network_comparison, "GraphSpace_Delaunay_Proximity.png", width = 10, height = 10)
```

## Compare labeled edge sets

Canonical edge keys preserve cell identity when checking shared and unique
pairs. The subset result and edge counts are calculated from this render's
data rather than copied from a previous run.

```{r labeled-edge-comparison, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
edge_keys <- function(graph) {
  edges <- igraph::as_data_frame(graph, what = "edges")
  paste(pmin(edges$from, edges$to), pmax(edges$from, edges$to), sep = "|")
}
delaunay_keys <- edge_keys(gs_crop_dnay@graph)
proximity_keys <- edge_keys(gs_crop_prox@graph)
edge_comparison <- data.frame(
  metric = c("Delaunay edges", "Proximity edges", "Shared edges", "Delaunay only", "Proximity only"),
  value = c(length(delaunay_keys), length(proximity_keys),
            length(intersect(delaunay_keys, proximity_keys)),
            length(setdiff(delaunay_keys, proximity_keys)),
            length(setdiff(proximity_keys, delaunay_keys)))
)
knitr::kable(edge_comparison)
cat("Every proximity edge is also a Delaunay edge:", all(proximity_keys %in% delaunay_keys))
write.csv(edge_comparison, file.path(result_dir, "network-edge-comparison.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r network-overlay, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
network_overlay <- ggplot() +
  edge_layer(gs_crop_dnay, colour = "grey45", alpha = 0.6) +
  edge_layer(gs_crop_prox, colour = "#cf3b36", alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point(data = gs_crop_dnay@nodes, aes(x = x, y = y), colour = "black", size = 0.2, pch = 19) +
  coord_equal() + theme_minimal() + labs(
    title = "Delaunay (grey) and proximity (red) networks",
    x = "Tissue coordinate 1", y = "Tissue coordinate 2"
  )
network_overlay
save_figure(network_overlay, "GraphSpace_Network_Overlay.png", width = 8, height = 7)
```

# Setting the proximity distance {#sec-setting-distance}

Based on `Vignettes/SettingDist_proximityNetwork.Rmd`.

Explore thresholds from 0 to 0.002 in increments of 0.0001. The candidate
distance table from Chapter 3 makes this sweep inexpensive. Store plots in a
list so that each entry remains a complete ggplot object.

## Build the distance sweep

```{r distance-sweep, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
edges_by_dist <- data.frame(dist = distance_grid, edges = integer(length(distance_grid)))
sweep_plots <- vector("list", length(distance_grid) + 1L)
sweep_plots[[1L]] <- plot_cells(
  gs_crop, polygons = FALSE, colour_by_expression = FALSE, title = "Cell proximity: no edges"
)
sweep_started <- Sys.time()
for (i in seq_along(distance_grid)) {
  gs_prox <- gs_neighbors(gs_crop, dist = distance_grid[i])
  edges_by_dist$edges[i] <- igraph::ecount(gs_prox@graph)
  sweep_plots[[i + 1L]] <- plot_cells(
    gs_prox, polygons = FALSE, edges = TRUE, colour_by_expression = FALSE,
    edge_colour = "#cf3b36", title = sprintf("Cell proximity: distance = %.4f", distance_grid[i])
  )
}
sweep_seconds <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), sweep_started, units = "secs"))
stopifnot(all(diff(edges_by_dist$edges) >= 0L))
knitr::kable(edges_by_dist, digits = 4, caption = "Edges at each polygon distance threshold")
cat(sprintf("Graph construction and plot preparation: %.2f seconds", sweep_seconds))
write.csv(edges_by_dist, file.path(result_dir, "edges-by-distance.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Save frames and render the animation

The frame directory is created in the shared setup. PNG dimensions match the
GIF dimensions. The animation includes all tested thresholds, starting at zero.

```{r distance-animation, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
frame_files <- vapply(seq_along(sweep_plots), function(i) {
  path <- file.path(frame_dir, sprintf("frame_%03d.png", i))
  ggplot2::ggsave(path, plot = sweep_plots[[i]], width = 6, height = 6,
                  units = "in", dpi = 120, bg = "white")
  path
}, character(1))
gif_file <- file.path(figure_dir, "CellProx_Dist.gif")
gifski::gifski(
  png_files = frame_files[-1L], gif_file = gif_file,
  width = 720, height = 720, delay = 0.2, progress = FALSE
)
knitr::include_graphics(gif_file)
```

## Relate distance to network size and cell diameter

Reuse the mean diameter from Chapter 2. The diameter ratio expresses the
threshold relative to polygon size in the same normalized coordinate system.

```{r distance-summary, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
edge_count_plot <- ggplot(edges_by_dist, aes(x = dist, y = edges)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#285e67") + geom_point(colour = "#285e67", size = 1.5) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = proximity_threshold, linetype = 2, colour = "#cf3b36") +
  theme_minimal() + labs(x = "Polygon distance threshold", y = "Number of edges")
edge_count_plot
save_figure(edge_count_plot, "Proximity_Distance_NumberEdges.png", width = 8, height = 4.5)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  selected_distance = proximity_threshold,
  mean_polygon_diameter = meanMaxDist,
  distance_to_diameter_ratio = proximity_threshold / meanMaxDist
), digits = 6)
```

# Visualizing direct neighbors {#sec-direct-neighbors}

Based on `Vignettes/Visualizing_DirectNeighbors.Rmd`.

Reuse the proximity graph built in Chapter 3. First compare an edge-only view
with edges over the segmentation polygons; then focus on a smaller region and
vary the edge and node rendering.

## View the neighbor network

```{r direct-neighbor-network, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
direct_neighbor_views <- plot_cells(
  gs_crop_prox, polygons = FALSE, edges = TRUE, colour_by_expression = FALSE,
  edge_colour = "#cf3b36", title = "Direct neighbor edges"
) + plot_cells(
  gs_crop_prox, nodes = FALSE, edges = TRUE, edge_colour = "#cf3b36",
  edge_alpha = 0.3, title = "Edges over cell segmentation"
) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")
direct_neighbor_views
save_figure(direct_neighbor_views, "DirectNeighbors_Overview.png", width = 11, height = 5)
```

## Crop and normalize the close-up

```{r direct-neighbor-crop, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
gs_neig2 <- cropGraphSpace(
  gs_crop_prox, xmin = 0.45, xmax = 0.6, ymin = 0.2, ymax = 0.35
)
stopifnot(nrow(gs_neig2@nodes) > 0L)
gs_neig2 <- normalizeGraphSpace(gs_neig2, mar = 0, norm.geometry = TRUE)
closeup_edges <- plot_cells(
  gs_neig2, nodes = FALSE, edges = TRUE, edge_colour = "#cf3b36",
  edge_alpha = 0.8, title = "Direct neighbors in the cropped region",
  edge_engine = "graphspace"
)
closeup_edges
save_figure(closeup_edges, "DirectNeighbors_Edges1.png", width = 7, height = 4)
```

## Compare edge rendering

Retain the vignette's arrow type and transparent-node experiment. Both variants
use the same plotting function defined in Chapter 1.

```{r direct-neighbor-rendering, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
gs_edge_attr(gs_neig2, "arrowType") <- "13|-|13"
rendering_variants <- list(
  plot_cells(gs_neig2, nodes = FALSE, edges = TRUE, edge_alpha = 0.8,
             title = "Arrow type 13|-|13", edge_engine = "graphspace"),
  plot_cells(gs_neig2, nodes = TRUE, edges = TRUE, edge_alpha = 0.8,
             node_size = 15, node_alpha = 0, title = "Transparent node layer",
             edge_engine = "graphspace")
)
for (i in seq_along(rendering_variants)) {
  print(rendering_variants[[i]])
  save_figure(rendering_variants[[i]], sprintf("DirectNeighbors_Edges%d.png", i + 1L),
              width = 7, height = 4)
}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  closeup_cells = nrow(gs_neig2@nodes), closeup_edges = igraph::ecount(gs_neig2@graph)
))
```

## Reproducibility and output checks

The output checks verify the main analysis tables, generated figures, frame
files, animation, graph consistency, and threshold sweep. Package versions and
session information are saved alongside the result tables.

```{r final-checks, eval = TRUE, echo = TRUE}
stopifnot(
  nrow(spatial_metrics) == length(cell_names),
  identical(as.character(gs_vertex_attr(gs_crop_dnay, "name")), cell_names),
  identical(as.character(gs_vertex_attr(gs_crop_prox, "name")), cell_names),
  igraph::is_simple(gs_crop_dnay@graph), igraph::is_simple(gs_crop_prox@graph),
  all(diff(edges_by_dist$edges) >= 0L),
  all(file.exists(frame_files)), file.exists(gif_file), file.info(gif_file)$size > 0
)
capture.output(sessionInfo(), file = file.path(result_dir, "session-info.txt"))
write.csv(data.frame(
  dataset = basename(data_file), md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(data_file)),
  selected_distance = proximity_threshold, maximum_distance = maximum_distance,
  mean_polygon_diameter = meanMaxDist
), file.path(result_dir, "render-inputs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  output = c("Figures and animation", "Animation frames", "Analysis tables and session information"),
  directory = c("Book/figures", "Book/frames", "Book/results")
))
sessionInfo()
```

## References and source vignettes

The five source vignettes are `InspectingNeighbors.Rmd`, `polygonGeometry.Rmd`,
`DelaunayNet.Rmd`, `SettingDist_proximityNetwork.Rmd`, and
`Visualizing_DirectNeighbors.Rmd`, all in the project's `Vignettes` directory.

For the spatial graph and geometry APIs, see the
[RGraphSpace nested geometries tutorial](https://sysbiolab.github.io/RGraphSpace/articles/nested-geometries.html),
[GraphSpace accessors and transformations](https://sysbiolab.github.io/RGraphSpace/articles/graphspace-accessors.html),
and the [sf geometric predicate reference](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/reference/geos_binary_pred.html).
The HTML is produced with [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-basics.html).
